To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NKA is found at the interface between two phases of the membrane and that its function is correlated with membrane softening.
(i) the spatial distribution of Na(+)/k(+)-ATPases in lipid bilayer membrane depends on the membrane phase and (ii) the activity of Na(+)-ATP-ases leads to softening the membrane.
the spatial distribution of NKA is influenced by the phase behavior of the membrane, and that its activity leads to a softening of the lipid membrane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interrelation of membrane phase, protein orientation and activity.
the spatial organization of proteins within lipid bilayer membranes and how it is related to the membrane phase and function of the protein.
the spatial arrangement of NKA in membranes of defined composition and the impact of the protein function on the membrane properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NKA activity is strongly affected by membrane phase and that the spatial distribution of NKA is determined by membrane phase.
the spatial distribution of the NKA in the membrane is determined by the lipid composition, and the membrane activity is determined by the spatial distribution of NKA.
the activity of the membrane protein depends on its spatial distribution in the membrane.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the activity of NKA in lipid bilayers depends on the phase composition of the membrane and the spatial distribution of NKA.
NKA is located at the lo/ld interface in GUVs with two-phase domains.
the activity of NKA depends on the lipid phase, the protein is located at phase boundaries, and that the activity leads to membrane softening.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the spatial distribution of the NKA in a two-phase membrane is not random but is determined by the phase boundary and that the NKA is oriented with its cytoplasmatic domain facing the lo phase and the extracellular domain facing the ld phase.
the spatial distribution of NKA depends on the lipid phase, and the protein activity leads to membrane softening.
NKA activity is coupled to membrane phase, and that the protein function can be used to control membrane adhesion to solid supports.
